filters.name: Create Symmetric Dodecahedron
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a Dodecahedron, but triangulated with an additional vertex in the middle of each face to preserve symmetry.

filters.name: Create Box
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a Box, Cube, Hexahedron. You can specify the side length.

parameters.label: Side Length
parameters.help: Length of each side of the box.

filters.name: Create Annulus
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create an Annulus e.g. a flat region bounded by two concentric circles, or a holed disk.

parameters.label: Inner Radius
parameters.help: Inner radius of the annulus.

parameters.label: Outer Radius

parameters.label: Sides

filters.name: Create Sphere
filters.shortDescription: Creates a Sphere by recursive subdivision of an Icosahedron.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a Sphere, whose topology is obtained as regular subdivision of an icosahedron.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.help: Radius of the sphere.

parameters.label: Subdivision Level
parameters.help: Number of recursive subdivisions. 0=icosahedron, 3=1280 faces, max=8.

filters.name: Create Sphere Cap
filters.shortDescription: Creates a triangulated unit-radius spherical cap from a refined hexagonal disk.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Creates a unit-radius spherical cap above the XY plane, with its circular boundary in the plane and its axis along +Z. The cap starts as a six-triangle disk; each subdivision splits every triangle into four, redistributes the interior vertices by Laplacian smoothing, and then lifts all vertices onto the sphere. This construction gives a regular, compact triangulation for shallow caps, but it is not a general-purpose spherical mesher. Triangle distortion grows toward the boundary for wide caps, becoming severe as the cap approaches a hemisphere.

**Cap Half-Angle** is the polar angle from the +Z axis out to the cap boundary, so it is half the cap's full angular diameter: 30° spans a 60° cap, and a hemisphere would be 90°. The filter stops at 89.5° because this disk-based parameterization degenerates at the hemisphere limit. For a well-shaped hemisphere or a wider spherical patch, start from a complete sphere and extract the required region instead.

parameters.label: Cap Half-Angle
parameters.help: Polar angle in degrees from the cap axis to its boundary, i.e. half the full angular diameter. A hemisphere would be 90°, where this construction degenerates.

parameters.label: Subdivision Level
parameters.help: Number of recursive refinements of the initial six triangles. Level n creates 6 × 4^n faces.

filters.name: Create Points on a Sphere
filters.shortDescription: Creates a point cloud distributed on a unit sphere.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a spherical point cloud, it can be random or regularly distributed.

parameters.label: Number of Points
parameters.help: Approximate number of points to generate.

parameters.label: Generation Technique
parameters.help: Strategy used to distribute points on the sphere.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the Monte Carlo point set exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Create Points on a Spherical Cap
filters.shortDescription: Creates an area-uniform point cloud on a unit-sphere cap.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Creates points on the surface of a unit-sphere cap centred on **Cap Direction** and bounded by **Cap Half-Angle** $\alpha$. Every generated point also receives its outward radial normal. Both techniques are uniform with respect to spherical surface area: equivalently, $\cos\theta$ is distributed uniformly in $[\cos\alpha,1]$, rather than $\theta$ being distributed uniformly. **Monte Carlo** generates independent random samples and can be reproduced with a non-zero seed. **Fibonacci** is deterministic and uses VCGLib's direct equal-area spherical-cap construction, producing the exact requested count without first generating and discarding points from a complete sphere. A half-angle of $180^\circ$ covers the complete sphere.

parameters.label: Number of Points
parameters.help: Exact number of points to generate.

parameters.label: Cap Direction
parameters.help: Direction from the sphere centre to the centre of the cap.

parameters.label: Cap Half-Angle
parameters.help: Polar angle in degrees from the cap axis to its boundary; 90 is a hemisphere and 180 covers the complete sphere.

parameters.label: Generation Technique
parameters.help: Random Monte Carlo sampling or deterministic Fibonacci sampling.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run; any other value makes Monte Carlo sampling exactly reproducible.

filters.shortDescription: Creates a Cone or truncated cone.

parameters.label: Bottom Radius
parameters.help: Radius of the bottom circle.

parameters.label: Top Radius
parameters.help: Radius of the top circle.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.help: Height of the cone.

parameters.label: Sides
parameters.help: Number of sides of the polygonal approximation.

filters.name: Create Cylinder
filters.shortDescription: Creates a cylinder of the given radius and height around an arbitrary axis.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Creates a cylinder centred on the origin, like **Create Cone** with equal radii but with a choice of axis and a tessellation that can be refined along its length.

*Sides* sets the angular tessellation; *Stacks* cuts the side wall into rings along the axis. One stack is enough for a cylinder that will only be rendered — add more when something downstream needs to deform or resample the side wall, since a single quad strip has no interior vertices to move.

*Axis* need not be normalized; only its direction is used, and the cylinder is always centred on the origin, spanning half the height either side.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.help: Radius of the cylinder.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.help: Length of the cylinder along its axis.

parameters.label: Sides
parameters.help: Number of sides of the polygonal approximation.

parameters.label: Stacks
parameters.help: Number of segments along the axis. One leaves the side wall as a single band of quads; raise it when the mesh will be deformed or resampled.

parameters.label: Close the ends
parameters.help: Add a flat cap at each end. Without them the result is an open tube.

parameters.label: Axis
parameters.help: Direction of the cylinder's axis. Need not be normalized, and its sign makes no difference: the cylinder is centred on the origin.

parameters.label: Horizontal Radius
parameters.help: Radius of the whole horizontal ring of the torus.

parameters.label: Vertical Radius
parameters.help: Radius of the vertical cross-section of the ring.

parameters.label: Horizontal Subdivisions
parameters.help: Subdivision steps around the ring.

parameters.label: Vertical Subdivisions
parameters.help: Subdivision steps of the cross-section circle.

filters.name: Create Plane from Selection
filters.shortDescription: Creates a quad on the plane fitting the current selection.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Fits a plane to the selected vertices (or vertices of selected faces) of the current mesh and creates a new planar quad mesh aligned to that plane.

parameters.label: Extent
parameters.help: Size of the plane relative to the selection bounding box on the plane. 1.0 = same size, 1.1 = 10% larger.

parameters.label: Subdivisions
parameters.help: Number of subdivisions along each side of the plane.

filters.name: Create Convex Hull
filters.shortDescription: Create the convex hull of the current mesh or point cloud.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Creates a new layer holding the **convex hull** of the current layer: the boundary of the smallest convex set containing all of its vertices.

Only the vertex positions are used, so this works on a point cloud just as well as on a mesh; faces, if any, are ignored. Every hull vertex is one of the input points, and interior points are discarded — which is why the result is a new layer rather than a modification of the current one.

At least 4 vertices are required, and they must not all be coincident, collinear, or coplanar.

Implemented with VCGLib's Quickhull.

Reference:
C. Bradford Barber, David P. Dobkin, Hannu Huhdanpaa, **The Quickhull Algorithm for Convex Hulls**, ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 22(4), 1996.
